runs.text: A calm companion between doctor visits
Challenge Statement 2 · AI Healthier Every Day
Scenario 1 · Mental health maintenance for working adults on antidepressants
“How might we build an AI-powered health companion that helps people understand and manage their medications, stay on track with their care, and take greater ownership of their long-term health?”
Problem statement · Healthcare track, NTU Lee Kong Chian School of Medicine
A dose gets missed, sleep drifts later, a flu knocks you out for a few days.
Most apps ask you to log your mood every evening, which is hard when you are tired or low.
When the appointment comes, it is all pieced together from memory.
A calm companion between doctor visits
A calm view for the patient; a clear “what changed and when” for the clinician they share with
written by AI from facts the system has checked
: sleep time later than usual since late February, and how the person has been checking in.
One tap a day, plain answers, honest limits
AURA asks what got in the way, because that is worth bringing to the doctor.
Can I take ibuprofen with it?
I'm not able to identify that medication, please check with your pharmacist.
AURA's exact reply in the live demo
, not made up by AI. When it can't answer, it says so.
Everything for the visit, in one place
What changed, when, and the missed dose with its reason, ready to discuss with the doctor or pharmacist.
Nothing is sent automatically · Not sent
WHAT THE CLINICIAN SEES · THE AGENT AT WORK
It decides what to look at, cites every statement, and is checked
What changed and when, with exact values and sources.
: which records it read, then “A second check reviewed 3 statements; all supported”. It can only read; it never changes the record or the treatment.
AURA notices resting heart rate is higher than in the person's
records, and says exactly that: a recent change, not a change from their usual.
When a change shows up, it offers
Anything a patient types is safety-checked first
If there is a concern, fixed safety resources take over the screen and the AI steps back. They are never AI-written.
The patient can't dismiss them. The clinician sees the same safety state when they open the record.
No alerts are sent in this prototype: who is told, and how fast, is for the care team to decide.
Asking to double a dose goes to safety, not to an answer.
Signals propose, rules decide, AI words it
— engines own personal baselines and safety; AI writes words and investigates.
Quiet patient surface, deep clinician inspection
— one record, two views; the patient decides what the clinician sees.
— numbers, dates and citations are checked plus an independent verifier; failures show related facts and say why.
— AI only matches a question to an approved topic.
Synthetic data now, private hosting later
— a hospital would run the model on its own infrastructure.
Six features the challenge asks for
Approved information about the person's own prescription; AI matches a question to an approved topic; honest “check with your pharmacist” when it can't answer
One tap a day: taken, not yet, skipped (no push reminders yet)
“What got in the way?” reasons, carried to the visit note
Wearable signals against the person's own usual and recent pattern
Refill and medication-review dates; screenings and vaccinations not yet
Visit note with changes and missed doses, Not sent until the patient decides
AURA describes changes; it does not predict relapse or give medication advice.
Core first, then the agent, then the experience
Safety and personal-baseline engines first, then the read-only agent, then the patient experience
AI development tools, including Tencent CodeBuddy and Miora, working from written specs
Every change reviewed and tested before release
write down what must never change before asking an AI to build anything.
IMPACT WE WOULD MEASURE IN A PILOT
Missed doses with a recorded reason
How many appointments start with a prepared note
Push reminders, screenings and pharmacist-reviewed content; consented real wearables; private hosting.
No diagnosis, relapse prediction or medication advice. Synthetic data only. Not clinically validated.
A calm companion between doctor visits, so both sides start the conversation on the same page.
